scope: Bangkok flood exposure and evacuation research
policy: A source is approved only when it is publicly accessible and has explicit reuse permission at resource level.

sources.authentication: Public registration and API key required
sources.notes: Approval applies to this resource, not automatically to every GISTDA disaster service.

sources.model_role: Independent water observation and flood-extent validation
sources.authentication: Free account may be required by delivery service
sources.licence: Copernicus data policy and legal notice
sources.notes: Use as an observation, never as a direct flood-depth measurement.

sources.model_role: Road, path, waterway and building network
sources.notes: Retain the extract date and checksum; provide OpenStreetMap attribution.
Thailand is covered. Height validation was not performed in Thailand; treat height as an estimate and locally validate.

sources.model_role: Population-at-risk estimate and synthetic-person seed totals
sources.notes: A gridded estimate is not a daytime activity population; demographic and activity marginals require separate evidence.

sources.agency: AWS Open Data (registry of open data on AWS) / Mapzen and upstream compilers
sources.dataset: Terrarium terrain tiles, global digital elevation
sources.model_role: Terrain elevation. LICENCE-APPROVED BUT NOT IN USE: the measured vertical accuracy is insufficient for flood depth, so no run ingests it.
sources.spatial_resolution: Approximately 19 m at zoom 13 for Bangkok; higher at greater zoom
sources.temporal_resolution: Static compilation of SRTM, NED, ETOPO and other upstream sources
sources.licence: Open data; upstream components are public domain or openly licensed. See the AWS registry entry for per-source attribution.
sources.notes: NOT USED IN ANY RUN. Licence passes, fitness fails. Measured: +5.0 m at the centre of the tile covering Khlong San, where ground is 1-2 m; a 32-sample transect across the Chao Phraya shows no river channel at all. Vertical error (about 5-10 m) exceeds the entire flood-relevant elevation range (0-2 m), so a stage-based depth surface built on it would be dominated by DEM noise. Open-Meteo elevation was tested as an alternative and is worse (8 m, same SRTM source). Copernicus DEM GLO-30/GLO-90 hosts do not resolve from this environment. To use terrain, obtain a vertical-accurate DEM through a reachable route; see docs/CITY_SCALE_LIMITATIONS.md.

sources.model_role: City-scale road, building and waterway geometry for the whole BMA
sources.temporal_resolution: Periodic extract; record the extract date and checksum
sources.notes: A single ~42 MB extract covers the whole metropolitan area, which is why city-scale ingestion does not need tiled Overpass queries. The extract date is a modelling parameter: the network version must record it.

sources.dataset: Thailand age and sex structures, 2026, R2025A
sources.model_role: Age/sex population marginals and vulnerability strata
sources.notes: Modelled aggregate estimates in age bands and by sex; do not treat cells as individual records or exact household composition. DOI: 10.5258/SOTON/WP00841.

sources.notes: Aggregate administrative controls. Record the downloaded resource URL, reporting date, geography crosswalk and checksum in each population build.

sources.agency: National Statistical Office / Department of Provincial Administration
sources.dataset: Registered population by area, sex and district, 2021–2025
sources.model_role: Population trend check and held-out district validation
sources.notes: Registered-population controls are not a daytime activity population. Preserve source-year and sex-category definitions.

sources.notes: Do not treat named locations as precise points unless coordinates are present and validated.

sources.agency: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (Copernicus Programme)
sources.dataset: Global Surface Water v1.4 yearly classification, 1984-2021
sources.model_role: OBSERVED surface-water extent; the only observational hazard layer available to the project
sources.format: GeoTIFF, 10 degree tiles, 40000x40000 at 0.00025 degree (about 30 m)
sources.notes: Landsat 5/7/8 derived water/non-water classification per year. Measures EXTENT, not depth, duration or direction. An annual composite under-detects short-lived inundation, so each year is a lower bound; 2011 is known to be poorly captured. A year cannot resolve within-year timing, so it cannot validate a 4-hour evacuation scenario directly, but it can validate spatial extent.

sources.agency: European Commission, Joint Research Centre / EC Copernicus
sources.dataset: Global Human Settlement Layer GHS-POP and GHS-BUILT-S
sources.model_role: Independent population and built-up cross-check against WorldPop and OSM footprints
sources.format: GeoTIFF (global archives are 12 GB per epoch; tile-level access required)
sources.spatial_resolution: 100 m (3 arc-second geographic or 100 m Mollweide)
sources.notes: Registered but NOT ingested. The catalogue is reachable and browsable, but the per-epoch archives are single 12 GB files with an empty tile subfolder, so an AOI-scoped pull is not yet demonstrated. Keep as verify until a real extract is produced.

sources.dataset: Provincial geohazard GIS bundle for Bangkok (DEM30m, contours, flood susceptibility, drainage basins, hydrography, roads)
sources.model_role: Mapped flood extent by year, drainage network and basins, overflow paths, flood-susceptible villages, and hydrography.
sources.format: ESRI shapefiles and a DSRB float32 grid
sources.temporal_resolution: Mixed; the flood layer carries years 2006, 2010, 2011
sources.licence: Restricted to social benefit, teaching, and disaster response. Chulalongkorn describes the maps as provided for free use for teaching AND disaster response; the Thai terms additionally prohibit use or modification for personal commercial benefit. This project is non-commercial flood-exposure research for disaster-response purposes, which falls inside the stated grant.
sources.notes: APPROVED BY PROJECT DECISION 2026-09-30: the maintainer overrode the earlier licence rejection on the stated basis that the use is disaster response, which Chulalongkorn explicitly names as a permitted purpose. The full terms remain recorded above so the decision is auditable. NOTE: this approval covers the hazard, drainage and hydrography layers ONLY. The bundled DEM and its contours remain EXCLUDED on fitness grounds, which are independent of licence: the DEM reads +13.8 m at Khlong San where ground is 1-2 m, with adjacent 30 m samples swinging 5-31 m across a floodplain with about 1 m of true relief. It is the same SRTM lineage already rejected. The accompanying .tif is a uint8 reclassification (0/74/255) and is not an elevation raster.
